analysis: Examined the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift patch (tool-call streaming for `auto` mode, a refactored terminal-info helper, and a modelType parameter passed to ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix) and the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump. I found no concrete regression. The new streaming path (head ~1366-1393) keeps the failure handling of the base path: finishToolCalls and ToolConstraintValidation.validate errors call releaseBox.fire() and finish the stream with the error, so the reservation and lease are released. The success path also fires releaseBox. Terminal usage is emitted through the extracted yieldTerminalInfo with the same fields as the base, including cachedPromptTokens from usageSignal, so no new prefix-cache or usage data is exposed (T-041/SEC-035 unchanged). The refactor adds no plaintext leak path: output still flows through the same continuation, which is encrypted downstream (T-008 is not touched here). The streaming path emits `auto` tool-call deltas before the whole call set is validated. Each call is validated when its frame closes, and the whole set is re-checked after the stream ends. A call that fails the set-level check at the end would already have been streamed to the consumer. This affects consumer-visible integrity of tool output from a model, and it is not a provider-trust or confidentiality boundary change, so I did not report it. Only the patch for lines 1190-1500 was visible, so I could not see ToolConstraintValidation, router.streamsToolCalls, finishToolCalls or the `streamedCalls:` init semantics. The modelType argument to streamingPrefix is defined elsewhere. The submodule bump from 889fe3c to 756432c contains unreviewable changes to the mlx-swift-lm dependency (inference engine, T-050/TB-007 surface). That diff is not supplied, so it is a coverage gap. Later passes should check the mlx-swift-lm diff for changes to the KV cache or SSD tier, memory handling, and tool parsing.
